rows.stem: Observe the given figure and select the statement that correctly states how these fungi obtain nutrition.

options.label: A
options.text: By eating the bread on which it is growing.

options.label: B
options.text: By using nutrients from the bread to prepare their own food.

options.label: C
options.text: By breaking down the nutrients of bread outside the body and then absorbing them.

options.label: D
options.text: By allowing other organisms to grow on the bread and then consuming them.

rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - a drawing of a slice of bread carrying bread mould, labelled 'Bread mould', 'Fungi body' and 'Bread'; the stem and options already say the fungi grow on bread, so the row is answerable from text. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
Bread mould is a fungus, a saprophyte. It cannot make its own food. It releases digestive enzymes onto the bread, breaks down the food material outside its body, and then absorbs the simple, digested nutrients.

This is option (C) By breaking down the nutrients of bread outside the body and then absorbing them.

rows.stem: If the part ‘P’ of the flower is removed, which of the following processes will not take place ?
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a longitudinal section of a flower (stamens, petals, a hatched pistil with round bodies in its swollen base, thalamus) with one label 'P'; which part P points at exists only in the drawing and is withheld here because it is the answer. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
P points at the swollen base of the pistil, the ovary, which holds the ovules. After fertilisation the ovary develops into the fruit, so if P is removed no fruit can form.

The ovules inside the ovary are what become the seeds, so removing the ovary removes the ovules too, and seed formation would also stop. That reading can equally be defended. The marking scheme reads P as the part that becomes the fruit.

The marking scheme's answer is option (C) Formation of fruit.

rows.stem:
Given below are some of the statements regarding our environment :

(i) Change in our life-styles have resulted in greater amounts of waste material generation.

(ii) Changes in attitude have resulted in use of more disposable things.

(iii) Changes in packaging has resulted in much of our waste becoming non-biodegradable.

(iv) Organic farming.

Which amongst these is not leading to any damage of environment ?
rows.solution:
Statements (i), (ii) and (iii) describe changes in life-style, attitude and packaging that increase waste, much of it non-biodegradable, and so harm the environment. Organic farming avoids chemical fertilisers and pesticides, so it does not damage the environment.

This is option (B) (iv).

rows.stem:
Identify the traits that cannot be transmitted from parents to the off-springs :

(i) Swimming technique

(ii) Blood group

(iii) Eye colour

(iv) Dancing skills

Options :
rows.solution:
Blood group and eye colour are controlled by genes, so they are inherited. Swimming technique and dancing skills are acquired during a person's lifetime; they bring no change in the DNA of the germ cells, so they cannot be passed on to the offspring.

This is option (B) (i) and (iv).

rows.subtopic: Human Brain and Protection of Nervous Tissue
rows.stem:
Following are the statements about the different parts of the brain. Select the correct statements.

(i) The thinking part of the brain is the forebrain.

(ii) Centres for smell, hearing, memory, sight are located in forebrain.

(iii) Salivation, vomiting, blood pressure are controlled by medulla in the hind brain.

(iv) Cerebellum does not control the posture and balance of the body.
rows.solution:
The forebrain is the main thinking part of the brain and has the centres for smell, hearing, sight and memory, so (i) and (ii) are correct. The medulla in the hind-brain controls involuntary actions such as salivation, vomiting and blood pressure, so (iii) is correct. The cerebellum does control posture and balance, so (iv) is incorrect.

This is option (A) (i), (ii) and (iii).

rows.stem:
Two pea plants, one with round green seeds (RRyy) and another with wrinkled yellow (rrYY) seeds were crossed with each other which produced \(\mathrm{F_1}\) progeny that have only round yellow (RrYy) seeds. When \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants are self-pollinated, the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) progeny will have which new combination of characters, as compared to the parents :

(i) Round, yellow

(ii) Round, green

(iii) Wrinkled, yellow

(iv) Wrinkled, green

Correct options are :
rows.solution:
The parents had round green seeds and wrinkled yellow seeds. In the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation the traits for seed shape and seed colour are inherited independently, so four kinds of seeds appear: round yellow, round green, wrinkled yellow and wrinkled green (\(9 : 3 : 3 : 1\)).

Round green and wrinkled yellow are the parental combinations. Round yellow and wrinkled green are the new combinations.

This is option (B) (i) and (iv).

rows.stem: In human beings the oxygen rich blood is pumped out to the body by :
rows.solution:
Oxygen-rich blood from the lungs enters the left atrium and passes into the left ventricle. The thick-walled left ventricle then contracts and pumps the blood out to the body through the aorta.

This is option (D) contraction of left ventricle.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Variations are not often seen in off-springs produced by asexual reproduction.

**Reason (R) :** DNA molecule generated by replication is not similar to the original DNA.
rows.context: Question Nos. 8 & 9 consists of two statements : Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option from (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
In asexual reproduction the offspring get the DNA of a single parent, so only small variations arise and the offspring are very similar to the parent. The Assertion is true.

DNA copying is a very accurate process: the copy is similar to the original, although it may not be absolutely identical. The Reason says the copy is not similar, so the Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Highest percentage of pesticides is found in tertiary consumers in a food chain.

**Reason (R) :** Chemicals / pesticides get accumulated progressively at each trophic level.
rows.context: Question Nos. 8 & 9 consists of two statements : Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option from (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Pesticides are not degradable, so they get accumulated progressively at each trophic level (biological magnification). The tertiary consumers sit at the highest level of the food chain, so the concentration of pesticides is maximum in them. The Assertion is true, and the Reason is true and explains it.

Both are true and the Reason is the correct explanation, which is option (A).

rows.stem:
“Transpiration in plants is a necessary evil.”

Comment on the statement giving two reasons.
rows.solution:
Transpiration is "necessary" because it creates the suction that pulls water and dissolved minerals up from the roots to the leaves, and it also helps to regulate the temperature of the plant.

It is an "evil" because the plant loses a large amount of water through it.

rows.stem: Explain why food chains generally consist of three or four steps.
rows.solution:
Only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is transferred to the next level; most of it is used for life processes and lost as heat. For example, if grass traps 1000 kJ, the grasshopper gets about 100 kJ and the frog only about 10 kJ.

So after three or four trophic levels very little usable energy is left, and a further level could not be supported. Food chains therefore generally have only three or four steps.

rows.stem: Varun is diabetic. His latest ultrasound reports showed a blockage in his pancreatic duct. How will this affect the dual functioning of the pancreas ?
rows.solution:
The pancreas has two functions. As an exocrine gland it sends pancreatic juice (with enzymes such as trypsin for proteins, lipase for fats and amylase for carbohydrates) through the pancreatic duct into the small intestine. With the duct blocked, these enzymes cannot reach the small intestine, so the digestion of proteins, carbohydrates and fats will be affected.

As an endocrine gland it secretes insulin directly into the blood, not through the duct. Varun is diabetic, so his insulin secretion is already affected; the blockage does not change this function.

rows.stem: Sunil unconsciously touched the hot iron rod and immediately withdrew his hand. Which type of action is involved ? Also define this action. Draw a flow chart to show the path followed for this action.
rows.solution:
It is a reflex action.

A reflex action is a sudden, automatic and quick response to a stimulus, which does not involve thinking.

Flow chart:

Stimulus (heat of the rod) \(\rightarrow\) receptor (in the skin) \(\rightarrow\) sensory neuron \(\rightarrow\) relay neuron (in the spinal cord) \(\rightarrow\) motor neuron \(\rightarrow\) effector (muscles of the arm) \(\rightarrow\) response (the hand is withdrawn)

rows.stem:
Give reasons for the following :

(a) Adrenal gland is known as the stress gland of the body.

(b) Prenatal sex determination is banned in India.

(c) Vegetative propagation is advantageous in some plants.
rows.solution:
(a) The adrenal gland secretes adrenaline, which prepares the body to deal with a scary or stressful situation (it makes the heart beat faster and sends more blood to the muscles). So it is called the stress gland.

(b) Prenatal sex determination is banned to prevent female foeticide, which disturbs the sex ratio of the population.

(c) Any one: plants raised by vegetative propagation bear flowers and fruits earlier than those grown from seeds; it allows plants such as banana, orange, rose and jasmine, which have lost the capacity to produce seeds, to be propagated; all the plants produced are genetically similar to the parent and have all its characteristics.

rows.stem:
Study the given table and answer the following questions :

| Parents | \(\mathrm{F_1}\) | \(\mathrm{F_2}\) |
|---|---|---|
| A pea plant with red flowers was crossed with a pea plant with white flowers. | 30 seeds were sown and all bore plants with red flowers. | 44 seeds were sown, 33 plants bore red flowers and 11 plants bore white flowers. |

(a) Depict the information given in the table in the form of a cross.

(b) Deduce the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) phenotypic ratio/\(\mathrm{F_2}\) ratio showing external look as well as genotypic /genetic makeup, ratio.
rows.solution:
(a) Red is dominant, since all the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants are red. Let R be the gene for red and r for white.

Parents: RR (red flowers) \(\times\) rr (white flowers)

Gametes: R and r

\(\mathrm{F_1}\): Rr, all with red flowers.

\(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants are self-pollinated: Rr \(\times\) Rr. Each gives gametes R and r.

| Gametes | R | r |
|---|---|---|
| R | RR (red) | Rr (red) |
| r | Rr (red) | rr (white) |

\(\mathrm{F_2}\): RR, Rr, Rr, rr, that is 3 red to 1 white.

(b) Phenotypic ratio (external look): 33 red : 11 white \(= 3 : 1\).

Genotypic ratio (genetic make-up): RR : Rr : rr \(= 1 : 2 : 1\).

rows.stem: Why is hydrotropism essential for plants ?
rows.context: Plants exhibit movements in response to various environmental stimuli to adopt and survive in their surroundings. These movements, influenced by external factors such as light, gravity, water and chemicals are regulated by specific plant hormones. For example, the differential growth of plant parts allows them to bend, grow or orient themselves in particular directions. Roots and shoots often show contrasting response to the same stimulus, highlighting the complex mechanisms involved in plant growth and development.
rows.solution: Hydrotropism makes the roots grow towards the area where water is available, so the plant can absorb water and the minerals dissolved in it.

rows.stem: What role does auxin play in the growth of plants ?
rows.context: Plants exhibit movements in response to various environmental stimuli to adopt and survive in their surroundings. These movements, influenced by external factors such as light, gravity, water and chemicals are regulated by specific plant hormones. For example, the differential growth of plant parts allows them to bend, grow or orient themselves in particular directions. Roots and shoots often show contrasting response to the same stimulus, highlighting the complex mechanisms involved in plant growth and development.
rows.solution: Auxin promotes cell elongation. It regulates tropic responses such as the bending of the stem towards light: auxin collects on the shaded side, those cells grow longer, and the shoot bends towards the light.

rows.stem: Differentiate between movement shown by the sensitive plant and tropic movement by plants (Two points).
rows.context: Plants exhibit movements in response to various environmental stimuli to adopt and survive in their surroundings. These movements, influenced by external factors such as light, gravity, water and chemicals are regulated by specific plant hormones. For example, the differential growth of plant parts allows them to bend, grow or orient themselves in particular directions. Roots and shoots often show contrasting response to the same stimulus, highlighting the complex mechanisms involved in plant growth and development.
rows.solution:
Any two:

| Movement in the sensitive plant | Tropic movement |
|---|---|
| Not directional; it does not depend on the direction of the stimulus. | Directional; it is towards or away from the stimulus. |
| Fast. | Slow. |
| Independent of growth (cells change shape by changing their water content). | Growth-related. |

rows.stem: How does movement of roots differ from that of shoots in response to gravity and light ?
rows.context: Plants exhibit movements in response to various environmental stimuli to adopt and survive in their surroundings. These movements, influenced by external factors such as light, gravity, water and chemicals are regulated by specific plant hormones. For example, the differential growth of plant parts allows them to bend, grow or orient themselves in particular directions. Roots and shoots often show contrasting response to the same stimulus, highlighting the complex mechanisms involved in plant growth and development.
rows.solution:
| | Roots | Shoots |
|---|---|---|
| Gravity | Grow towards gravity (positive geotropism). | Grow away from gravity (negative geotropism). |
| Light | Grow away from light (negative phototropism). | Grow towards light (positive phototropism). |

rows.stem:
(a) Draw a labelled diagram showing open and closed stomatal pore.

(b) List the main events that occur during the process of photo-synthesis.

(c) Write a balanced chemical equation showing photo-synthesis in plants.
rows.solution:
(a) Draw two stomata side by side. Open stomatal pore: two kidney-shaped guard cells, swollen and curved apart, leaving a wide pore between them, each with chloroplasts. Closed stomatal pore: the two guard cells shrunk and straight, pressed together so that the pore is closed. Label the guard cells, the stomatal pore and the chloroplasts, and name the two drawings "open" and "closed".

(b) The main events of photosynthesis:

1. Absorption of light energy by chlorophyll.

2. Conversion of light energy into chemical energy, and splitting of water molecules into hydrogen and oxygen.

3. Reduction of carbon dioxide to carbohydrates.

(c) \(\mathrm{6CO_2 + 12H_2O \xrightarrow[\text{Sunlight}]{\text{Chlorophyll}} C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 + 6H_2O}\)

\(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\) is glucose.

rows.stem:
(a) Draw a well-labelled diagram of nephron and label atleast 4 of its parts.

(b) Write the role of capillary cluster inside Bowman’s capsule.

(c) What is meant by selective reabsorption ?
rows.solution:
(a) Draw a nephron: a cup-shaped Bowman's capsule at the top holding a cluster of capillaries (the glomerulus), which is supplied by a branch of the renal artery; from the capsule a long, coiled tubular part runs down and loops back up, surrounded by capillaries that drain into a branch of the renal vein; the tubule opens into a collecting duct. Label at least four of: Bowman's capsule, glomerulus, tubular part of the nephron, collecting duct, branch of renal artery, branch of renal vein, capillaries.

(b) The capillary cluster (glomerulus) filters the blood. Water, glucose, salts, amino acids and nitrogenous wastes such as urea pass from the blood into the Bowman's capsule, so the wastes are removed from the blood.

(c) Selective reabsorption is the process in which useful substances in the filtrate, such as glucose, amino acids, vitamins, salts and most of the water, are taken back into the blood as the filtrate flows along the tubule, while the wastes are left to form urine.

rows.stem: The volume ratio of hydrogen and oxygen gases liberated during electrolysis of water is
rows.solution:
In the electrolysis of water, \(\mathrm{2H_2O \rightarrow 2H_2 + O_2}\). Two molecules of hydrogen form for every molecule of oxygen, so the volume of hydrogen collected is twice the volume of oxygen.

This is option (B) 2 : 1.

rows.stem:
\(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_{6(aq)} + 6O_{2(g)} \longrightarrow 6CO_{2(g)} + 6H_2O_{(l)}}\).

The above reaction is an example of -
rows.solution:
This is the oxidation of glucose (respiration). It releases energy, so it is an exothermic reaction.

This is option (C) Exothermic Reaction.

rows.stem: An aqueous solution turns red litmus blue. Excess addition of which of the following solution would reverse the change ?
rows.solution:
A solution that turns red litmus blue is basic. To reverse the change, the solution must become acidic so that the blue litmus turns red again. An excess of an acid does this; sodium hydroxide, baking soda and slaked lime are all basic.

This is option (B) Hydrochloric acid.

rows.stem: While washing dirty clothes by soap, micelles are formed. Select the correct statement about micelles.

options.label: A
options.text: The hydrophobic tail of the soap molecule is in the interior of the cluster, whereas hydrophilic end is on the surface of the cluster.

options.label: B
options.text: The hydrophobic tail is on the surface of the cluster, whereas hydrophilic end is in the interior of cluster.

options.label: C
options.text: Both hydrophobic tail and hydrophilic end are in the interior of the cluster.

options.label: D
options.text: Both hydrophobic tail and hydrophilic end are on the surface of the cluster.

rows.solution:
In a micelle the hydrocarbon (hydrophobic) tails of the soap molecules point inwards, into the oily dirt, while the ionic (hydrophilic) ends face outwards into the water.

This is option (A) The hydrophobic tail of the soap molecule is in the interior of the cluster, whereas hydrophilic end is on the surface of the cluster.

rows.stem: Which one of the following metals does \(\underline{\text{not}}\) react with cold water ?
rows.solution:
Sodium and potassium react violently with cold water, and calcium reacts with it less vigorously. Magnesium does not react with cold water; it reacts with hot water.

This is option (D) Magnesium.

rows.stem: Alloys are homogeneous mixture of metal with a metal or non-metal. Which among the following alloys contain non-metal as one of its constituents ?
rows.solution:
Steel is an alloy of iron with carbon, a non-metal. Brass (copper and zinc), bronze (copper and tin) and amalgam (mercury with another metal) contain only metals.

This is option (D) Steel.

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem: How will you protect yourself from the heat generated while diluting a concentrated acid ?

options.label: A
options.text: By adding acid to water with constant stirring.

options.label: B
options.text: By adding water to acid with constant stirring.

options.label: C
options.text: By adding water to acid followed by base.

options.label: D
options.text: By adding base to acid with constant stirring.

rows.solution:
Diluting a concentrated acid is highly exothermic. The acid must be added slowly to water with constant stirring, so the heat spreads through the large volume of water. Adding water to the acid can make the mixture boil and splash out the acid.

This is option (A) By adding acid to water with constant stirring.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Pure ethanoic acid is also known as glacial acetic acid.

**Reason (R) :** Pure ethanoic acid often freezes during winter due to its low melting point of 290 K.
rows.context: In the question, two statements are given – One labelled as Assertion (A) and other labelled as Reason (R). Write the correct answer selecting the appropriate option from (A), (B), (C) & (D) given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Pure ethanoic acid is called glacial acetic acid, so the Assertion is true.

Its melting point is 290 K (about 17 \(^\circ\)C), so in cold places it often freezes in winter, and the frozen acid looks like ice; this is why it is called glacial. The marking scheme follows the NCERT text and reads the Reason as true and as the explanation.

Strictly, the word "low" in the Reason is misplaced: it is the relatively high melting point of 290 K, above winter temperatures, that makes the acid freeze in winter. Read that way, the Reason as worded would be false.

The marking scheme's answer is option (A), both true with the Reason explaining the Assertion.

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem:
(a) A compound ‘A’ is used in soda-lime fire-extinguisher and decomposes on heating to form compound ‘B’. Compound ‘B’ is used for removing permanent hardness of water. Identify ‘A’ and ‘B’.

(b) Write chemical formula of Plaster of Paris. At what temperature gypsum is heated to obtain Plaster of Paris ?
rows.solution:
(a) A is sodium hydrogen carbonate (baking soda), \(\mathrm{NaHCO_3}\). On heating it decomposes into B:

\(\mathrm{2NaHCO_3 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Na_2CO_3 + H_2O + CO_2}\)

B is sodium carbonate, \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}\) (as washing soda, \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\)), which is used to remove the permanent hardness of water. (The extinguisher NCERT describes is the soda-acid type.)

(b) Plaster of Paris is \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O}\). Gypsum is heated at 373 K (100 \(^\circ\)C) to obtain it.

rows.stem:
Account for the following :

(a) White silver chloride turns grey when exposed to sunlight.

(b) Lead (II) nitrate on heating releases brown fumes.

(c) Bags of oil and fat containing food items are flushed with nitrogen gas.
rows.solution:
(a) In sunlight, silver chloride decomposes into silver and chlorine. The grey colour is the silver formed.

\(\mathrm{2AgCl(s) \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} 2Ag(s) + Cl_2(g)}\)

(b) On heating, lead(II) nitrate decomposes and gives off nitrogen dioxide, which is a brown gas.

\(\mathrm{2Pb(NO_3)_2(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2PbO(s) + 4NO_2(g) + O_2(g)}\)

(c) Nitrogen is an unreactive gas. Flushing the bags with it keeps out oxygen and so prevents the oxidation of the fats and oils, which would make the food rancid.

rows.stem:
(i) Which method will be used to convert each of them to their respective metal oxides ?

(a) Carbonate ore

(b) Sulphide ore

(ii) Write a chemical reaction to illustrate the use of aluminium for joining cracked railway tracks.

(iii) During extraction of metals, electrolytic refining is used to obtain pure metals. Which material will be used as anode and cathode for the refining of copper metal by this process ?
rows.solution:
(i) (a) A carbonate ore is converted to its oxide by calcination, that is, heating strongly in a limited supply of air:

\(\mathrm{ZnCO_3(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} ZnO(s) + CO_2(g)}\)

(b) A sulphide ore is converted to its oxide by roasting, that is, heating strongly in the presence of excess air:

\(\mathrm{2ZnS(s) + 3O_2(g) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2ZnO(s) + 2SO_2(g)}\)

(ii) In the thermit reaction, aluminium reduces iron(III) oxide; so much heat is produced that the iron formed is molten and is used to join the cracked rails.

\(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3(s) + 2Al(s) \rightarrow 2Fe(l) + Al_2O_3(s)}\) + heat

(iii) Anode: a thick rod of impure copper. Cathode: a thin strip of pure copper. (The electrolyte is a solution of acidified copper sulphate.)

rows.stem:
(i) Write all the reactions involved in the extraction of Zn from ZnS.

(ii) Hydrogen gas is not evolved when most of the metals react with nitric acid. Give reason.
rows.solution:
(i) Zinc blende is first roasted, converting the sulphide into the oxide:

\(\mathrm{2ZnS(s) + 3O_2(g) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2ZnO(s) + 2SO_2(g)}\)

The zinc oxide is then reduced to zinc by heating with carbon:

\(\mathrm{ZnO(s) + C(s) \rightarrow Zn(s) + CO(g)}\)

(ii) Nitric acid is a strong oxidising agent. It oxidises the hydrogen produced to water and is itself reduced to oxides of nitrogen (\(\mathrm{N_2O}\), NO, \(\mathrm{NO_2}\)). (Only magnesium and manganese give hydrogen with very dilute nitric acid.)

rows.stem: What type of indicator is used to predict how strong an acid or base is ?
rows.context: The pH plays an important role in our daily life. Strength of acids and bases depends on the number of \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions and \(\mathrm{OH^-}\) ions produced by these respectively. pH scale helps in predicting the strength of acids and bases by measuring hydrogen ion concentration in a solution.
rows.solution: A universal indicator, which shows different colours at different concentrations of hydrogen ions.

rows.stem: Three solutions A, B and C showed pH as 3, 5 and 7. Which solution has the highest concentration of \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions ?
rows.context: The pH plays an important role in our daily life. Strength of acids and bases depends on the number of \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions and \(\mathrm{OH^-}\) ions produced by these respectively. pH scale helps in predicting the strength of acids and bases by measuring hydrogen ion concentration in a solution.
rows.solution: Solution A (pH 3). The lower the pH, the higher the concentration of \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions.

rows.stem: What are strong acids and weak acids ?
rows.context: The pH plays an important role in our daily life. Strength of acids and bases depends on the number of \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions and \(\mathrm{OH^-}\) ions produced by these respectively. pH scale helps in predicting the strength of acids and bases by measuring hydrogen ion concentration in a solution.
rows.solution: Strong acids give a large number of \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions in water, for example hydrochloric acid. Weak acids give fewer \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions in water, for example acetic acid.

rows.stem:
(i) Under what condition is rainwater called acid rain ?

(ii) In the following acids, identify weak acids :

Nitric acid, hydrochloric acid, acetic acid, sulphuric acid, formic acid.
rows.context: The pH plays an important role in our daily life. Strength of acids and bases depends on the number of \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions and \(\mathrm{OH^-}\) ions produced by these respectively. pH scale helps in predicting the strength of acids and bases by measuring hydrogen ion concentration in a solution.
rows.solution:
(i) When the pH of rainwater falls below 5.6, it is called acid rain.

(ii) The weak acids are acetic acid and formic acid.

rows.stem:
(i) Carbon cannot form \(\mathrm{C^{4+}}\) cation and \(\mathrm{C^{4-}}\) anion. Explain.

(ii) Define homologous series of carbon compounds. Why are the melting and boiling points of \(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}\) higher than \(\mathrm{C_3H_8}\) or \(\mathrm{C_2H_6}\) ?

(iii) What happens when ethanol is heated with acidified potassium dichromate ?
rows.solution:
(i) To form \(\mathrm{C^{4+}}\), carbon would have to lose four electrons, which needs a very large amount of energy. To form \(\mathrm{C^{4-}}\), it would have to gain four electrons, and a nucleus with six protons cannot hold ten electrons. So carbon forms neither ion, and shares its electrons instead (covalent bonds).

(ii) A homologous series is a series of compounds in which the same functional group substitutes for hydrogen in a carbon chain; successive members differ by a \(\mathrm{-CH_2-}\) unit.

Melting and boiling points increase with molecular mass in a series. \(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}\) has a higher molecular mass than \(\mathrm{C_3H_8}\) or \(\mathrm{C_2H_6}\), so its melting and boiling points are higher.

(iii) Ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid (acetic acid), and the orange colour of the dichromate turns green.

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{acidified } K_2Cr_2O_7,\ \text{heat}} CH_3COOH}\)

rows.stem:
(i) How would you name the following :

I. \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}CHO}\)

II. \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}C{\equiv}CH}\)

(ii) When ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid in the presence of conc. \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\), a substance with sweet smell is produced. Answer the following :

I. State the class of compounds to which the sweet smelling compounds belong.

II. Write the chemical equation for the reaction.

(iii) Why soaps do not produce foam with hard water ?
rows.solution:
(i) I. Propanal. II. Propyne.

(ii) I. Esters.

II. \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH + CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{acid}} CH_3COOCH_2CH_3 + H_2O}\)

The product is ethyl ethanoate.

(iii) Hard water contains calcium and magnesium salts. Soap reacts with them to form an insoluble substance called scum, so it does not produce foam.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: The pair of eye parts responsible for admitting different amount of light in to the eyes is
rows.solution:
The iris controls the size of the pupil, and the pupil is the opening through which light enters the eye. Together they regulate the amount of light admitted.

This is option (A) Iris and pupil.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem: The vision defect which arises due to gradual weakening of the ciliary muscles and diminishing flexibility of eye lens is :
rows.solution:
With age, the ciliary muscles weaken and the eye lens loses its flexibility, so the power of accommodation decreases and near objects cannot be seen clearly. This defect is presbyopia.

This is option (C) Presbyopia.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** With the help of compass, magnetic field lines can be traced outside the bar magnet.

**Reason (R) :** The north pole of a compass needle always points towards the south pole of the magnet when brought close to it.
rows.context: Direction : For question number 32, two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to this question from the codes (A), (B), (C) & (D) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
A compass needle placed at different points near a bar magnet lines up along the magnetic field there, so marking its positions traces the field lines outside the magnet. The Assertion is true.

Near the magnet the north pole of the needle is attracted by the south pole of the magnet, so the Reason is true as a statement. The marking scheme takes it as the explanation.

Strictly, a compass traces field lines because the needle aligns with the local field at each point, not because its north pole "always" points at the south pole; that holds only close to that pole. On that reading the Reason, though true, does not explain the Assertion.

The marking scheme's answer is option (A), both true with the Reason explaining the Assertion.

rows.stem: A fuse in electric circuit is rated 4 A. Can it be used with an electric heater of rating 2 kW, 200 V ? Explain your answer.
rows.solution:
Current drawn by the heater:

\(I = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{2000}{200} = 10\) A.

The heater draws 10 A, much more than the 4 A rating of the fuse. The fuse would melt and break the circuit, so it cannot be used with this heater.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem: How is an electromagnet made ? Write any two ways by which the strength of electromagnet can be increased.
rows.solution:
An electromagnet is made by winding a coil of insulated copper wire around a core of a magnetic material such as soft iron, and passing a current through the coil (that is, by placing a soft iron core inside a current-carrying solenoid).

Its strength can be increased by increasing (i) the number of turns in the coil and (ii) the current flowing through the coil.

rows.stem:
(a) Define volt, the unit of potential difference.

(b) Calculate the work done required to move an electron between two points A and B located at a potential difference of 100 V in an electric field.
rows.solution:
(a) One volt is the potential difference between two points in a current-carrying conductor when 1 joule of work is done to move a charge of 1 coulomb from one point to the other: \(1\,\mathrm{V} = \dfrac{1\,\mathrm{J}}{1\,\mathrm{C}}\).

(b) \(V = \dfrac{W}{Q}\), so \(W = QV\).

The charge on an electron is \(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\) C, so

\(W = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 100 = 1.6 \times 10^{-17}\) J.

rows.stem:
(a) Observe the given ray diagram and compare :

(i) the speed of light in medium A and the speed of light in medium B.

(ii) the optical densities of medium B and medium C.

(b) Draw a ray diagram for refraction where the optical density of medium ‘A’ becomes equal to the optical density of medium ‘C’ and optical density of medium ‘B’ is greater than the optical density of medium ‘A’ and medium ‘C’.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - (a) is answered only from the printed ray diagram: a rectangular block labelled Medium 'B' with Medium 'A' above it and Medium 'C' below it; a ray from A strikes the top face where a dashed normal N is drawn, with angles i and r marked, crosses the block and leaves through the bottom face into C. How the ray bends at each face is withheld here because it decides both comparisons. Page idx 26.
rows.solution:
(a) (i) On entering medium B, the ray bends towards the normal (r is smaller than i), so B is optically denser than A. The speed of light in medium A is greater than the speed of light in medium B.

(ii) The ray passes from B into C without bending, so media B and C have the same optical density.

(b) This is the case of a glass slab in air. Draw a rectangular block for medium B with medium A above and medium C below. A ray from A falls obliquely on the top face; draw the normal there. Inside B the ray bends towards the normal. At the bottom face draw another normal; the ray leaves into C bending away from the normal. Since A and C have the same optical density, the emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray, shifted sideways (produce the incident ray with a dotted line to show the shift). Mark the angles of incidence and refraction at both faces and the arrows on the rays.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: Explain the phenomenon of rainbow formation in the sky. Draw the labelled ray diagram in support of your explanation.
rows.solution:
A rainbow is caused by the dispersion of sunlight by tiny water droplets present in the atmosphere after a rain shower. Each droplet acts like a small prism: it refracts and disperses the incident sunlight, then reflects it internally, and finally refracts it again as it comes out of the drop. The colours emerge spread out, and an observer with the sun behind sees a rainbow.

Diagram: draw a circular raindrop. A ray of white sunlight enters the drop and is refracted and split into colours; the colours are reflected from the back of the drop and are refracted again as they leave, with red and violet coming out separately. Label the white sunlight, the raindrop, red and violet, and put arrows on the rays.

rows.stem:
On the basis of the given circuit arrangement, answer the following questions :

(a) What happens to the rod AB when the key K is closed and why ?

(b) Name and state the rule that determines this behaviour of the rod AB in the above situation.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the question is built on the printed set-up and gives no description of it: a horseshoe magnet with poles marked S (upper arm) and N (lower arm), a rod with ends A and B hung by two wires from a horizontal arm on a stand so that it lies between the poles, and a circuit of a battery and a key K. The sense of the current through AB is shown only by arrows and is withheld here. Page idx 26.
rows.solution:
(a) When the key K is closed, the rod AB is displaced (it moves sideways) from its original position. A current-carrying conductor placed perpendicular to a magnetic field experiences a force, at right angles to both the field and the current; reversing the current would reverse the displacement.

(b) Fleming's left-hand rule. Stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, the thumb points in the direction of the motion of, or the force on, the conductor.

rows.stem: What kind of image of a star is seen by the observer in the eye-piece ?
rows.context: The above ray diagram is to show image formation by a reflecting telescope. Reflecting telescope revolutionized our way of looking into the sky. Reflecting telescopes employ large mirrors to gather and focus light rather than relying solely on lenses as we do in the refracting telescopes. These telescopes utilize precisely shaped and polished mirrors to capture incoming light and reflect it to a focal point, where the telescope forms an image for observation.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the passage refers to 'the above ray diagram': a tube admitting 'Parallel Light Rays from distant star', a large mirror at the far end labelled 'Curved Mirror', a small inclined 'Plane Mirror' in the tube, and an 'Eye-piece' lens in a side tube below. The shapes of the curved mirror and of the eye-piece lens are withheld here because they answer (b) and (c). Page idx 28.
rows.solution:
A magnified image of the star. The curved (concave) mirror collects the parallel rays from the star and forms a real image of it at its focus; the eye-piece magnifies this image. The marking scheme accepts either "real" or "magnified".

"Real" describes the image formed by the mirror. The final image seen through the eye-piece is formed by a converging lens acting as a magnifier, so it is virtual and magnified.

rows.stem: What kind of mirror is used in this reflecting telescope ?
rows.context: The above ray diagram is to show image formation by a reflecting telescope. Reflecting telescope revolutionized our way of looking into the sky. Reflecting telescopes employ large mirrors to gather and focus light rather than relying solely on lenses as we do in the refracting telescopes. These telescopes utilize precisely shaped and polished mirrors to capture incoming light and reflect it to a focal point, where the telescope forms an image for observation.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the passage refers to 'the above ray diagram': a tube admitting 'Parallel Light Rays from distant star', a large mirror at the far end labelled 'Curved Mirror', a small inclined 'Plane Mirror' in the tube, and an 'Eye-piece' lens in a side tube below. The shapes of the curved mirror and of the eye-piece lens are withheld here because they answer (b) and (c). Page idx 28.
rows.solution: A concave (converging) mirror is the curved mirror that gathers and focuses the light; a plane mirror is also used, to turn the reflected rays towards the eye-piece.

rows.stem: Explain with the reason, what kind of optical device (type of lens or mirror) is used at the eye-piece.
rows.context: The above ray diagram is to show image formation by a reflecting telescope. Reflecting telescope revolutionized our way of looking into the sky. Reflecting telescopes employ large mirrors to gather and focus light rather than relying solely on lenses as we do in the refracting telescopes. These telescopes utilize precisely shaped and polished mirrors to capture incoming light and reflect it to a focal point, where the telescope forms an image for observation.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the passage refers to 'the above ray diagram': a tube admitting 'Parallel Light Rays from distant star', a large mirror at the far end labelled 'Curved Mirror', a small inclined 'Plane Mirror' in the tube, and an 'Eye-piece' lens in a side tube below. The shapes of the curved mirror and of the eye-piece lens are withheld here because they answer (b) and (c). Page idx 28.
rows.solution: A convex lens is used at the eye-piece. It is a converging lens, and it magnifies the image formed by the curved mirror so that the distant star can be seen enlarged.

rows.stem: What is the role of plane mirror in image formation by this telescope ?
rows.context: The above ray diagram is to show image formation by a reflecting telescope. Reflecting telescope revolutionized our way of looking into the sky. Reflecting telescopes employ large mirrors to gather and focus light rather than relying solely on lenses as we do in the refracting telescopes. These telescopes utilize precisely shaped and polished mirrors to capture incoming light and reflect it to a focal point, where the telescope forms an image for observation.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the passage refers to 'the above ray diagram': a tube admitting 'Parallel Light Rays from distant star', a large mirror at the far end labelled 'Curved Mirror', a small inclined 'Plane Mirror' in the tube, and an 'Eye-piece' lens in a side tube below. The shapes of the curved mirror and of the eye-piece lens are withheld here because they answer (b) and (c). Page idx 28.
rows.solution: The plane mirror reflects the light rays coming from the curved mirror and redirects them sideways towards the eye-piece, so that the image is formed where the observer can view it, outside the main tube.

rows.stem:
(i) The given electric circuit is a part of an electrical device. Use the information given in the electric circuit diagram to calculate :

(I) Potential difference across the ends of resistor \(\mathrm{R_2}\).

(II) Value of resistor \(\mathrm{R_2}\).

(III) Value of resistor \(\mathrm{R_1}\).

(ii) Write the factors on which resistance of a conductor depends and derive the formula for resistance of a given conductor.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - every value (i) needs is printed only on the circuit diagram: a 12 V battery and key K in series with a resistor R1, a parallel pair (a 4.0 Ω resistor marked 1.5 A, and R2) and a 2.0 Ω resistor, with 2.0 A marked on the main line on both sides of the parallel pair. Page idx 30.
rows.solution:
(i) Let the total current be I = 2.0 A, the current through the \(4.0\,\Omega\) resistor \(I_1 = 1.5\) A and the current through \(\mathrm{R_2}\) be \(I_2\).

(I) \(\mathrm{R_2}\) is in parallel with the \(4.0\,\Omega\) resistor, so the potential difference across it is the same:

\(V = I_1 R = 1.5 \times 4.0 = 6\) V.

(II) \(I_2 = I - I_1 = 2.0 - 1.5 = 0.5\) A.

\(\mathrm{R_2} = \dfrac{V}{I_2} = \dfrac{6}{0.5} = 12\,\Omega\).

(III) Potential difference across the \(2.0\,\Omega\) resistor: \(V = IR = 2.0 \times 2.0 = 4\) V.

Potential difference across \(\mathrm{R_1}\) \(= 12 - (6 + 4) = 2\) V.

\(\mathrm{R_1} = \dfrac{V}{I} = \dfrac{2}{2.0} = 1\,\Omega\).

(Check: the parallel pair is \(\dfrac{4 \times 12}{4 + 12} = 3\,\Omega\), so the total resistance is \(1 + 3 + 2 = 6\,\Omega\), and \(\dfrac{12}{6} = 2\) A, as marked.)

(ii) The resistance of a conductor depends on its length, its area of cross-section and the nature of its material (and on temperature).

Resistance is directly proportional to the length: \(R \propto l\).

Resistance is inversely proportional to the area of cross-section: \(R \propto \dfrac{1}{A}\).

Combining, \(R \propto \dfrac{l}{A}\), so \(R = \rho\dfrac{l}{A}\), where \(\rho\) is a constant of proportionality called the resistivity of the material.

rows.stem:
(i) How much electric current will an electric iron draw from 220 V source if the resistance of its heating element when hot, is \(55\,\Omega\) ? Calculate the power consumed by the electric iron when it is operated at 220 V.

(ii) In a house, 3 bulbs of 100 watt each, are lit for 5 hours daily and an electric heater of 1.0 kW is used for half an hour daily. Calculate the total energy consumed in a month of 30 days and its cost at the rate of ₹ 3.60 per kWh.

(iii) With reason explain, why are alloys commonly used to make elements of electrical heating devices.
rows.solution:
(i) \(I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{220}{55} = 4\) A.

Power, \(P = VI = 220 \times 4 = 880\) W.

(ii) Energy \(=\) power \(\times\) time.

Bulbs: \(3 \times 100 \times 5 = 1500\) Wh \(= 1.5\) kWh per day.

Heater: \(1.0 \times 0.5 = 0.5\) kWh per day.

Total per day \(= 1.5 + 0.5 = 2\) kWh.

In 30 days: \(30 \times 2 = 60\) kWh, that is 60 units.

Cost \(= 60 \times 3.60 =\) ₹ 216.

(iii) Alloys have a higher resistivity than their constituent metals, so they produce more heat, and they do not oxidise (burn) readily at high temperatures. So they are used for the heating elements.
